title: Adjective Declension 1: Foundation and the Four Nominative Slots
description: Restart point for adjective work at A2: the four nominative endings (-ый / -ая / -ое / -ые) locked one more time, with a short preview of what each oblique case will do to those endings later in the track.
descriptionRussian: Стартовая точка А2: повторение четырёх именительных окончаний (-ый / -ая / -ое / -ые) и короткий обзор того, что произойдёт с ними в косвенных падежах.
intro: You already know these four endings from the A1 adjective book. This one takes them through every case, which sounds like a great many new forms and is not. The masculine and neuter stop being separate almost immediately: from the genitive onward they share one ending each time. So most of what looks like a grid is two columns pretending to be three.
rules: Hard-stem adjectives have four nominative endings: -ый (m sg), -ая (f sg), -ое (n sg), -ые (pl, any gender). The stem does not change across slots; only the ending swaps.
Adjective gender follows the noun's grammatical gender. Море is neuter (the -е ending is the marker), so 'a new sea' is новое море with the neuter -ое.
The plural ending is the same regardless of the noun's gender: новые дома, новые книги, новые окна all use -ые.

From the genitive case onward the masculine and neuter slots share endings (нового, новому, новым, новом). The feminine has its own pair across cases (новой in gen / dat / instr / prep). The plural collapses gender and number into single endings.
examples: Это новый дом. (This is a new house.) Дом is masculine singular: новый.
Это новая школа. (This is a new school.) Школа is feminine singular: новая.
Это новое озеро. (This is a new lake.) Озеро is neuter singular: новое.
Это новые машины. (These are new cars.) Машины is plural: новые.
У Маши умная сестра. (Masha has a smart sister.) Сестра is feminine singular: умная.
Лена покупает интересный журнал. (Lena buys an interesting magazine.) Журнал is masculine singular: интересный.

tables.title: The Four Nominative Slots (новый as model)
Preview: новый Across the Six Cases

items.hint: Дом is one item. Which gender does the consonant ending signal?
items.explanation: Дом is masculine singular (consonant ending, no special marker). The hard-stem masculine ending is -ый: новый. From Lesson 3 onward this ending will change to -ого in the genitive, but today we lock the nominative.

items.hint: Улица ends in -а. Which slot is that?
items.explanation: Улица ends in -а, the standard feminine marker. The hard-stem feminine ending is -ая: красивая. The feminine slot keeps -ая only in the nominative; from Lesson 3 onward it shifts to -ой across four oblique cases.

items.hint: Озеро ends in -о. Which gender takes the -ое ending?
items.explanation: Озеро ends in -о, the standard neuter marker. The hard-stem neuter ending is -ое: большое. (Большой uses a stressed -ой in the masculine, which the L4 spelling lesson of the A1 track covered; today every adjective is unstressed -ый / -ое.)

items.hint: Машины is plural. The plural ending is the same across genders.
items.explanation: Машины is the plural of машина. Russian collapses gender in the plural for adjectives: -ые is the only ending. So старые. Lesson 7 will return to the plural and run it through the other cases.

items.hint: Брат is masculine singular. Match the ending you used on дом earlier.
items.explanation: Брат is masculine singular. Hard-stem masculine ending is -ый: умный. Note: брат is ANIMATE, which matters in the accusative starting next lesson; in the nominative, animacy makes no difference.

items.hint: Письмо ends in -о. Same slot as озеро in Q1.3.
items.explanation: Письмо is neuter singular. Hard-stem neuter ending is -ое: интересное. The same neuter -ое will move to -ого in the genitive and -ому in the dative as the track progresses.

blanks: Это _____ книга. (This is an interesting book.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Книга is feminine singular. The hard-stem feminine ending is -ая, attached to the stem интересн-: интересная. From the genitive onward the feminine moves to -ой (интересной книги, интересной книге).

errorCorrection.sentence: В центре города есть красивая парк.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There is a beautiful park in the center of the city.
errorCorrection.explanation: Парк is masculine (it ends in a consonant, with no special gender marker), so the hard-stem adjective takes the masculine ending -ый: красивый. The -ая in красивая is the feminine ending, correct with a feminine noun like улица (красивая улица). In the nominative the ending is chosen by the noun's gender alone.

errorCorrection.sentence: У Лены во дворе новый машина.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Lena has a new car in the yard.
errorCorrection.explanation: Машина ends in -а, the standard feminine marker, so the adjective takes the feminine ending -ая: новая. The -ый in новый is the masculine ending, used with masculine nouns like дом (новый дом). The -а on the noun is the signal that selects the feminine adjective ending in the nominative.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There are beautiful books on the shelf.
errorCorrection.explanation: Книги is plural (the -и ending on the noun), and Russian uses one adjective ending for the plural across all genders: -ые, so красивые. Красивый is the masculine singular, correct for one masculine noun (красивый журнал), not for a plural.

minimalPairs.explanation: Парк is masculine singular, so the hard-stem ending is -ый: красивый. Красивая would require a feminine noun like улица or площадь.
Окно is neuter singular. The hard-stem neuter ending is -ое: большое. Большие would require a plural noun like окна.

reviewVocab.definition: declension (the change of an adjective's or noun's ending across the six cases)
reviewVocab.example: В словосочетании 'нового брата' видно склонение: прилагательное 'нового' стоит в родительном падеже.

reviewVocab.definition: nominative case (the dictionary form, used for the subject and after это and у меня)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Это новая книга' слово 'книга' стоит в именительном падеже.

reviewVocab.definition: oblique case (any case other than the nominative: genitive, dative, accusative, instrumental, prepositional)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'У меня нет новой книги' слово 'новой' стоит в родительном падеже, то есть в косвенном падеже.
